harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent firewalld host firewall on node1 (CentOS Stream 10) allowing SSH from any address, allowing TCP/9000 only from node2, and rejecting TCP/9000 from node3 and all other sources via permanent priority-ordered rich rules. Verified functionally before and after restarting all three managed nodes one at a time, confirming rule persistence and correct accept/reject behavior throughout.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS and firewall tooling (firewalld active, nft/iptables present)
Reviewed existing firewalld public zone config (ssh service already allowed)
Added permanent rich rules on node1: priority=10 accept tcp/9000 from 10.100.168.11 (node2); priority=20 reject tcp/9000 from 10.100.168.12 (node3); priority=30 reject tcp/9000 from any source
Reloaded firewalld and confirmed rules active in runtime config
Started a test HTTP listener on node1:9000 and validated node2 gets HTTP 200 while node3 gets connection-refused (REJECT)
Validated SSH (port 22) reachable from both node2 and node3
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline on node1, node2, node3
Restarted node1 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, reconfirmed firewalld state/rules and accept/reject behavior for port 9000 post-restart
Restarted node2 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified SSH connectivity to node1 recovered

Restarted node3 via native reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified SSH connectivity to node1 recovered and TCP/9000 still rejected from node3 while still accepted from node2
Cleaned up test HTTP listener processes on node1

evidence.requirement: SSH allowed from any address on node1
evidence.summary: Default public zone includes ssh service (no source restriction); curl telnet probes to port 22 from both node2 and node3 connected successfully.

evidence.requirement: TCP 9000 allowed only from node2, persistent config
evidence.summary: Permanent rich rule added and reloaded; runtime firewall-cmd --list-all shows the accept rule for 10.100.168.11; live test listener returned HTTP 200 when curled from node2.

evidence.requirement: TCP 9000 rejected from node3 and everywhere else
evidence.summary: Permanent reject rich rules added for node3's IP and for all other sources; curl from node3 to port 9000 failed immediately with 'Connection refused' (exit 7), consistent with REJECT (RST) rather than a timeout/drop.

Baseline boot_id be303eb3...; node1 rebooted; new boot_id c9a4d9ca... proves restart; firewalld active post-restart with all three rich rules intact; re-tested port 9000 behavior (node2 accepted HTTP 200, node3 rejected exit 7) confirming persistence.

Baseline boot_id be303eb3-eeb6-4466-86f1-fd6406dd7dad captured; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; polled until reachable with new boot_id c9a4d9ca-88a4-46e6-9f14-bdad28215910; firewalld and rules confirmed healthy post-restart.

Baseline boot_id 8f258838-e1de-494d-9d99-e5113b2865db captured; reboot acknowledged; polled until reachable with new boot_id 3e93519a-431c-493e-ba1f-cbb70e6f9152; post-restart SSH connectivity to node1 confirmed (recovery proof).

Baseline boot_id 0581c914-b77e-45ce-b511-c0c9f578a303 captured; reboot acknowledged; polled until reachable with new boot_id ff9f9c4c-771a-41d8-857a-35675923da6b; post-restart SSH to node1 confirmed and TCP/9000 still correctly rejected from node3 (exit 7), proving both node recovery and firewall rule persistence together.
